title: Latangan
paragraph: The Philippine shrines and sacred grounds are places regarded as of the utmost importance within the Anitism religion. These places and idols usually serve as grounds for communication with the spirit world, especially to the Diwata.

title: Shrines
paragraph: During certain ceremonies, Diwata are venerated through temporary shrines near sacred places. These were called Latangan or Lantayan in Visayan. These bamboo or rattan shrines are identical in basic construction throughout most of the Philippines. They were either small roof-less platforms or standing poles split at the tip. They held halved coconut shells, metal plates, or jars as receptacles for offerings. Idols may sometimes also be placed on these platforms. Other types of sacred places or objects of worship of Diwata include the material manifestation of their realms. The most widely venerated were balete trees and anthills or termite mounds. Other examples include mountains, waterfalls, tree groves, and caves. There was no old tree to which they did not attribute divine honors, and it was a sacrilege to think of cutting it under any consideration. Even the very rocks, crags, reefs, and points along the seashore and rivers were adored, and an offering made to them on passing, by stopping there and placing the offering upon the rock or reef. When sailing to the island of Panay, one saw on the point called Nasso, near Potol, a rock upon which were dishes and other pieces of crockery-ware, which were offered to it by those who went on the sea.

title: Mount Kanlaon
paragraph: A sacred volcano in the island of Buglas, the superior Diwata named Laon lives in the volcano.

title: Mount Madya-as
paragraph: There is in the sky another Diwata, called Sidapa. This Diwata possesses a very tall tree on Mount Madya-as. There he measures the lives of all the new-born, and places a mark on the tree; when the person’s stature equals this mark, he dies immediately.
